title: Remove the Pigment, or Remove the Cell

scenes.tts: To learn what a part is for, take it away. But which part should you take away?
scenes.visual: Title card: Remove the Pigment, or Remove the Cell. The two-inputs, one-exit diagram with three pairs of scissors hovering. Question on screen: which part?
scenes.narration: To learn what a part is for, take it away. But which part should you take away?

scenes.tts: The one idea gives three choices. Remove the pigment. Remove the rods and cones. Or remove the cell.
scenes.visual: Scissors labelled: melanopsin; rods and cones; the cell.
scenes.narration: The one idea gives three choices. Remove the pigment. Remove the rods and cones. Or remove the cell.

scenes.tts: First, the readouts. For the clock, keep a mouse on a light-dark cycle and watch its running.
scenes.visual: A running-wheel record with a light-dark bar across the top.
scenes.narration: First, the readouts. For the clock, keep a mouse on a light-dark cycle and watch its running.

scenes.tts: A mouse entrains if its running keeps a fixed timing relative to the cycle.
scenes.visual: Running onsets line up under lights-off on every row. Label: entrains.
scenes.narration: A mouse entrains if its running keeps a fixed timing relative to the cycle.

scenes.tts: A mouse whose clock is not entrained free-runs. It drifts on its own internal period.
scenes.visual: A second record where the running onset slides a little each day, a diagonal across the rows. Label: free-runs.
scenes.narration: A mouse whose clock is not entrained free-runs. It drifts on its own internal period.

scenes.tts: Separately, a brief light pulse at night tests how far the rhythm phase-shifts.
scenes.visual: A light pulse marked on one night; the following rows' onsets step to a new time. Label: phase shift.
scenes.narration: Separately, a brief light pulse at night tests how far the rhythm phase-shifts.

scenes.tts: Masking is a third readout. Bright light at night often suppresses a mouse’s running right away, independently of any clock shift. The same light can also shift the clock.
scenes.visual: Bright light switched on during the dark part of a row; the running ticks thin out during the light. Label: masking, an acute activity change; measure clock phase separately.
scenes.narration: Masking is a third readout. Bright light at night often suppresses a mouse’s running right away, independently of any clock shift. The same light can also shift the clock.

scenes.tts: For the pupil, film the constriction over seconds to minutes of steady light.
scenes.visual: An eye under steady light; a pupil-size trace begins along a time axis marked in seconds to minutes.
scenes.narration: For the pupil, film the constriction over seconds to minutes of steady light.

scenes.tts: Row one is wild type. It entrains, shifts fully, and its pupil constricts fast and holds.
scenes.visual: Genotype table begins. Columns: relay, melanopsin, clock, pupil. Row 1, wild type: yes, yes, entrains with full shifts, fast and held. A pupil trace drops fast and stays down.
scenes.narration: Row one is wild type. It entrains, shifts fully, and its pupil constricts fast and holds.

scenes.tts: Row two has no melanopsin. It still entrains, but its phase shifts to brief pulses are smaller.
scenes.visual: Row 2, no melanopsin: yes, no, entrains with smaller shifts.
scenes.narration: Row two has no melanopsin. It still entrains, but its phase shifts to brief pulses are smaller.

scenes.tts: Its pupil constricts, but in steady bright light the constriction fades over minutes.
scenes.visual: Row 2 pupil trace: drops fast, then drifts back up over minutes. Label: fades.
scenes.narration: Its pupil constricts, but in steady bright light the constriction fades over minutes.

scenes.tts: Row three has no rod or cone signalling. It entrains. Its pupil is slower and less sensitive, but it holds.
scenes.visual: Row 3, no rod or cone signalling: no, yes, entrains. Its pupil trace drops slowly, then stays down.
scenes.narration: Row three has no rod or cone signalling. It entrains. Its pupil is slower and less sensitive, but it holds.

scenes.tts: In bright light, it reaches its normal maximum.
scenes.visual: Row 3 trace reaches the same depth as wild type in bright light.
scenes.narration: In bright light, it reaches its normal maximum.

scenes.tts: Row four is the triple mutant. It lacks melanopsin, rod transducin and a cone channel subunit.
scenes.visual: Row 4 labelled triple mutant: no Opn4, no Gnat1, no Cnga3. Relay: no. Melanopsin: no.
scenes.narration: Row four is the triple mutant. It lacks melanopsin, rod transducin and a cone channel subunit.

scenes.tts: It does not entrain. It free-runs, shows no masking and has no significant pupil reflex.
scenes.visual: Row 4 fills: does not entrain, free-runs, no masking; its pupil trace is flat.
scenes.narration: It does not entrain. It free-runs, shows no masking and has no significant pupil reflex.

scenes.tts: Read down the table. Either input alone is enough to entrain and to constrict. Lose both, and nothing is left.
scenes.visual: Rows 2 and 3 highlighted together, then row 4 alone.
scenes.narration: Read down the table. Either input alone is enough to entrain and to constrict. Lose both, and nothing is left.

scenes.tts: Predict. Keep the rods and cones working, and kill the I P R G Cs. If rods and cones had their own route, what would you see?
scenes.caption: Predict. Keep rods and cones working, and ablate ipRGCs. If rods and cones had their own route, what would you see?
scenes.visual: A fifth row, labelled hypothetical ablation: rods and cones intact, ipRGCs ablated. Clock and pupil cells left blank with question marks.
scenes.narration: Predict. Keep rods and cones working, and ablate ipRGCs. If rods and cones had their own route, what would you see?

scenes.tts: A strong separate route would let these mice keep much of their clock and pupil responses, like the melanopsin knockouts.
scenes.visual: A ghost version of row 2 slides into row 5, labelled: if a strong separate route existed.
scenes.narration: A strong separate route would let these mice keep much of their clock and pupil responses, like the melanopsin knockouts.

scenes.tts: Guler and colleagues found something else. The deficits were larger than with melanopsin loss alone, close to those of the triple mutants.
scenes.caption: Güler and colleagues found something else. The deficits were larger than with melanopsin loss alone, similar to those of the triple mutants.
scenes.visual: The ghost fades; row 5 fills with severe deficits close to row 4: impaired entrainment and a much-reduced pupil trace, not drawn identical to row 4. Label: Güler and colleagues, 2008; Opn4 disrupted by the toxin gene; incomplete ipRGC loss; some pupil response remained.
scenes.narration: Güler and colleagues found something else. The deficits were larger than with melanopsin loss alone, similar to those of the triple mutants.

scenes.tts: Pattern vision, which runs through other ganglion cells, remained.
scenes.visual: A small grating icon beside row 5, ticked: pattern vision remained.
scenes.narration: Pattern vision, which runs through other ganglion cells, remained.

scenes.tts: So in mice, these cells are the main route to the clock and the pupil.
scenes.visual: The single axon of the two-inputs diagram highlighted. Label: main route, in mice.
scenes.narration: So in mice, these cells are the main route to the clock and the pupil.

scenes.tts: An ablation removes both inputs, so it cannot say which input supplied what was lost.
scenes.visual: Side by side: knockout scissors cut one arrow; ablation scissors cut the whole cell. Label: different questions.
scenes.narration: An ablation removes both inputs, so it cannot say which input supplied what was lost.

scenes.tts: Predict. Here are made-up phase shifts. Do the two single losses add up to the loss of both?
scenes.visual: On screen: wild type 2.0 h; no melanopsin 0.6 h; no rods and cones 1.8 h; ablation 0 h. Made-up values.
scenes.narration: Predict. Here are made-up phase shifts. Do the two single losses add up to the loss of both?

scenes.tts: They do not. Together the two single losses are smaller than the loss when both inputs go.
scenes.visual: On screen: deficits 1.4 h + 0.2 h = 1.6 h, but losing both = 2.0 h. And 0.6 h + 1.8 h = 2.4 h, more than 2.0 h.
scenes.narration: They do not. Together the two single losses are smaller than the loss when both inputs go.

scenes.tts: One possible reading is that the output saturates. A pupil cannot get smaller than its minimum.
scenes.visual: A curve of output against total drive that rises and then flattens. Label: saturates.
scenes.narration: One possible reading is that the output saturates. A pupil cannot get smaller than its minimum.

scenes.tts: A phase shift has a ceiling too. Near a ceiling, the stronger input alone gets close, and adding the other gains little.
scenes.visual: On the curve, the rods-and-cones-alone point sits at 30% of the wild-type response (0.6 of 2.0 h) and the melanopsin-alone point at 90% (1.8 of 2.0 h). Label: one possible model; where it saturates is not known.
scenes.narration: A phase shift has a ceiling too. Near a ceiling, the stronger input alone gets close, and adding the other gains little.

scenes.tts: A single knockout shows what the other input can do alone. It does not show each input's share.
scenes.visual: Label: a knockout shows what the other input can do alone, not a share.
scenes.narration: A single knockout shows what the other input can do alone. It does not show each input's share.

scenes.tts: One limit. In the Guler mice, a weakened toxin gene at the melanopsin locus kills the cells gradually and incompletely, and more are lost with age.
scenes.caption: One limit. In the Güler mice, a weakened toxin gene at the melanopsin locus kills the cells gradually and incompletely, and more are lost with age.
scenes.visual: A timeline from birth to adult; cell loss starts early and grows with age. Label: germline ablation, gradual loss.
scenes.narration: One limit. In the Güler mice, a weakened toxin gene at the melanopsin locus kills the cells gradually and incompletely, and more are lost with age.

scenes.tts: Losing cells during development can let targets rewire. An ablation timed in adults is better.
scenes.visual: A second timeline with the ablation marked in adulthood. Label: adult-timed ablation.
scenes.narration: Losing cells during development can let targets rewire. An ablation timed in adults is better.

scenes.tts: Remove the pigment, and the relay carries on. Remove the cell, and both inputs go.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: knockout leaves one arrow; ablation leaves none. Text: two experiments, two different questions.
scenes.narration: Remove the pigment, and the relay carries on. Remove the cell, and both inputs go.
